title: How Long, O LORD? A Prayer From the Sickbed
summary: David, weak in body and shaken in soul, begs the LORD not to discipline him in anger but to heal and deliver him. He describes nights soaked in tears and eyes worn out by grief. Then, abruptly, his tone changes: the LORD has heard his weeping, and his enemies will be put to shame.

from.text: From early in Christian history the church grouped Psalm 6 with Psalms 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, and 143 as the seven Penitential Psalms, prayed especially in times of repentance and during Lent.

line: A man weak in body and shaken in soul begs God for mercy and healing, weeps through the night, and then, suddenly, knows that the LORD has heard his weeping.
guide: The psalm lets you ask God how long and leave the sentence unfinished; that is prayer too. Pray it as it is, without dressing it up, for yourself or for someone you love who cannot pray it tonight. Say verse 9 aloud, even before you feel it.

care.text: The psalm does not give his sorrow a medical name, and these notes do not give anyone's sorrow a name either. But if your nights are like the nights in this psalm, please do not carry them alone. Tell someone you trust: a doctor, a pastor, or a friend. When grief or sadness lasts and starts taking sleep, appetite or work, seeing a doctor is wise, and it is not a failure of faith. If you have thoughts of hurting yourself, please speak to someone now: a doctor, a pastor, a trusted friend, or a crisis line. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: Heading and plea: do not rebuke me in anger, heal me
Turn and save me, for the dead cannot praise you
Nights of weeping, eyes worn out with grief
The LORD has heard: the enemies turn back

verses.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments, according to Sheminith. A Psalm of David. O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.
Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are in agony.
My soul is deeply distressed. How long, O LORD, how long?
Turn, O LORD, and deliver my soul; save me because of Your loving devotion.
For there is no mention of You in death; who can praise You from Sheol?
I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping and drench my couch with tears.
My eyes fail from grief; they grow dim because of all my foes.
Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard my weeping.
The LORD has heard my cry for mercy; the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed; they will turn back in sudden disgrace.
